rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Biofield Tuning and the body's messages", "body": "Chance described the biofield anatomy he learned from Eileen Day McKusick, a field of roughly six feet around the body in which he said pockets of stuck energy can be located by sweeping a tuning fork through it. He said the location can point to a limiting belief or past trauma, and that he moved the energy back to the body and checked it. Chance said the body never does anything wrong and acts as a mirror, and that he did most sessions remotely. Chris said he had personally tried a remote session and valued it."}, {"title": "Victim consciousness and the inner world", "body": "Chance argued that spiritual growth and conspiracy research should be combined, with neither blaming outsiders for everything nor ignoring real manipulators. He described his view that limiting beliefs hold back life force energy, and that the same pattern could apply to humanity through mass ancestral trauma. Chance said the outer world does not direct the inner world, calling that belief victim consciousness. Chris described his own experience that focusing on the negative seemed to draw more of it, and that creativity brought synchronicities."}, {"title": "Demons as fragments of the self", "body": "When Chris asked how to integrate demons, Chance offered his perspective that the Greek word behind demon referred to the spirits of the dead rather than infernal imps. He suggested many experiences labeled as demons could be restless ancestral patterns or cut off parts of a person's own energy, while saying he was not ruling out independent entities. Chance recommended the book Soul Centered Healing by Tom Zinser. He also described anger as a polarity that, in his view, is healthiest when expressed in small honest amounts."}, {"title": "Gnostic misunderstandings and spirit in matter", "body": "Chris asked whether reality is natural or an overlay run by archons. Chance said he was fully at home in this reality and criticized what he called pop culture Gnosticism that treats the world as a prison. He described matter as condensed spirit, using the image of a seed becoming a tree, and said there was no separate spirit world. Chance also said the Greek word demiurge meant a public worker, and he read the Trinity and destroyer figures as seasonal nature symbols that were later misunderstood."}, {"title": "Constellation writing and the secret of letters", "body": "Chance described how ancient astronomer priests, including Sumerian priests who used the term Lumashi, derived scripture from constellation names, puns, and wordplay. He said being initiated meant having the secret of letters, and that savior figures such as the Logos or the God of eloquence symbolized it. Early on he described the Celtic Hercules Ogmios, a figure he said carried golden chains from his mouth to his followers' ears. Chance also gave his reading of Jehovah, Eve, and Jove as variant transliterations of the same four Hebrew letters."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I highly encourage you to check out this epic flow state chat with Chris at FKN, especially if you'd like a good overview of how tuning works, or the biggest misconceptions about Gnosticism.
